title: Where AI is superhuman: The right jobs to automate with LLMs
talk_summary: A VC's framework for where LLMs are superhuman: high-volume, low-complexity task-queue jobs where AI competes against rules-based automation, not humans. The actionable core is decomposing jobs to task/subtask level and targeting the high-volume queue work rather than complex planning.

takeaways.what_they_do: They classify jobs by volume vs complexity and target high-volume, low-complexity work whose primary interface is a task queue (alerts, CRM lists, repetitive messages), where LLMs beat rules-based systems rather than humans.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the primary interface is a task cue like a list of prospects in a CRM or a list of security alerts
takeaways.numbers: 40-70% of day-to-day work automatable in mid-complexity jobs

takeaways.what_they_do: Before automating, they break a workflow into explicit subtasks (e.g. choose tool, write query, debug errors) rather than treating a job as one monolithic prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we break down the workflows to a task or subtask level

takeaways.technique: AI vs rules-based baseline, not vs human
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue LLM systems only need to beat the previous rules-based automation, not a human expert, because volume makes 80-90% reliability still 10x better in aggregate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your competition is no longer AI versus human it's AI versus previous generation of rules-based software

takeaways.what_they_do: Agentic systems propagate a newly learned threat pattern to all customers instantly, unlike per-analyst human learning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they can share learnings across customers so if there's a new kind of threat that comes in all of the customers

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents constantly run variants and evaluate outcomes over time, discovering new cohorts/insights rather than following fixed rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agents are constantly running experiments of what to show to whom
